Mapping these cell-specific roles clarifies how the factor shapes learning, injury, and disease.
europmc-pmc6582859: A cut sets off a choreographed repair: first inflammation clears debris, then new tissue fills the gap, and finally remodeling strengthens the patch. This comprehensive review walks through each phase of skin wound healing and the cells and signals driving it. Understanding the choreography helps doctors nudge slow or stuck wounds toward closure.
europmc-pmc6600059: Oxidative stress - rogue oxygen molecules beating the body's defenses - harms sperm as surely as other cells. This systematic review examines how reactive oxygen species affect male fertility and what helps: testing methods, antioxidant treatments, and lifestyle fixes. The guidance helps clinicians evaluate and manage a common, missed cause of infertility.
europmc-pmc6615259: Infections can trigger depression-like behavior through brain inflammation - and melatonin may blunt it. In mice given bacterial toxin, the sleep hormone calmed overactive microglia and quieted the NLRP3 inflammasome, easing depressive-like symptoms. The study hints at an unexpected anti-inflammatory role for melatonin in mood.
europmc-pmc6667459: Mapping which proteins touch - via cross-linked peptides - needs serious computing. pLink 2 is a high-speed search engine for proteome-scale cross-link identification, running about 40 times faster than its predecessor. Proteomics researchers get answers in hours instead of weeks.
europmc-pmc6702459: Good health programs are designed, not improvised - but the design work is often invisible. Intervention Mapping is a step-by-step protocol for planning theory-based, evidence-backed health promotion, illustrated with real examples. The perspective piece shows planners how to move from good intentions to programs that actually work.
europmc-pmc6710759: Aging rusts us from within - oxygen's byproducts scar proteins and fats into compounds called ALEs and AGEs. This review traces how oxidative stress and these end products drive age-related decline. The chemistry of growing old, the authors argue, is largely the chemistry of slow burning.
europmc-pmc6711459: To map the brain's conversations, scientists model cause and effect between regions - that is Dynamic Causal Modelling. Part one of this guide covers first-level DCM analysis for fMRI: fitting the models to one person's data. The tutorial turns an intimidating method into a followable recipe.
europmc-pmc6744659: The m6A tag on RNA - a tiny methyl mark - behaves differently in every cancer. Surveying 33 cancer types, this study mapped how m6A regulators are altered and what that means for patients. The pan-cancer atlas turns a molecular detail into clinical insight.
europmc-pmc6770259: Curcumin promises much and delivers little - because the body barely absorbs it. This review tackles the bioavailability bottleneck: why the golden compound passes through unabsorbed and which formulations actually raise blood levels. The gap between hype and health, measured.
europmc-pmc6815659: Flu kills far more people than the old estimates admitted. This study tallied global flu deaths anew, finding 290,000 to 650,000 deaths yearly - well above WHO's earlier figures. The bigger toll demands bigger prevention. Counting the dead honestly is step one to saving lives.
europmc-pmc6823959: Genomics is swimming in data - millions of genomes on the way. This paper shows GPUs can scale number-crunching genomics to millions of people, cheap and fast. The gaming chips become lab tools. Borrowed horsepower for the data deluge.
europmc-pmc6835559: Apples and onions carry heart-friendly compounds - quercetin and kaempferol. This review examines their bioavailability and potential cardiovascular benefits in humans: how much reaches the blood, and what it does there. The produce aisle as pharmacy. Eat your colors - the science agrees.
europmc-pmc6893459: Obesity may start in the gut - and probiotics might help. This review weighs gut bugs and obesity: the case for probiotics in weight control. The tiny residents sway the waist. Feed the right bugs, trim the waist. The field is young but hopeful.
europmc-pmc6919559: Outlining cell cores is step one of image biology - a contest crowned the best. The 2018 Data Science Bowl took on core outlining across scan tests. The top code set the bar. Hordes of teams, one outlining duel. Shared research at its most fierce.
europmc-pmc7005859: Hundreds of protein maps, fast charted. This paper gives rapid, site-specific deep protein map charting by data-independent capture without boosting. The messaging speed-run. High-throughput cell messaging, remade. Repeatable across hundreds of samples. Going big was the task - now cracked. Counted protein mapping goes big.
europmc-pmc7013859: Toxin tripwires: LPS spotting surveyed. This review maps recent gains in LPS spotting nets: TLR4 and beyond. The germ alarm system. Gram-negative germ tiny mark. Everywhere germ-linked shape. Best-known PAMP in immune science. Inborn feeling starts here. Healing aiming at of TLR4 probed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-59: This 2007 GAO report grades U.S. trade deals struck under fast-track rules — the process that lets the White House cut pacts Congress then votes up or down. GAO checks whether the deal-makers heard out Congress and private firms as the law demands. The report gives Congress a scorecard on talks that shape jobs and prices at home.
gao-gaoreports-b-299859: Alpha Genesis challenged a 2007 federal award, and GAO's ruling gives the final answer. The firm said the bid process was unfair; the call tests each claim and closes the book. For research and service firms in the government market, the verdict is another line in the fair-bidding code.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-559: Handshake deals were hiding in the Pentagon's books in 2007 — GAO's report says open-ended contract actions were undercounted and slow to get finalized. The findings expose the paperwork limbo where billions sat. The report demands that handshake buying get real contracts, and get them fast.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-759: Tank-killing tech needed a fair trial in 2007 — GAO's report dissects how the Pentagon judged active protection systems for armored vehicles. The findings grade the evaluation game. The report asks whether the best shield won, or just the best-connected bidder.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-259: Reserve troops' job rights needed better policing in 2007, and GAO's report says more action was required to oversee employment protections. The findings demand the enforcement. The report's cause: those who serve should not lose their jobs for it. The uniform should not cost a career.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-59: Medicare's medical-equipment bills were full of errors in 2007, and GAO's report says improvements were needed to curb the improper payments. The findings target the waste. The report warns that the wheelchair invoices needed a closer look. The program was paying for ghosts.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-159: The District's buying system was broken in 2007, and GAO's report says the procurement setup needed major reform. The findings demand the overhaul. The report warns that the capital's contracts deserved better than chaos. The city had to buy like it meant it.
gao-gaoreports-b-298859: Squires Timber Company took its December 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Timber deals get the same full hearing as the tech ones.
gao-gaoreports-b-298759: Symetrics Industries took its October 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-859: Homeless veterans' programs needed better follow-up in 2006, and GAO's report says improved communication could enhance the grant program. The findings demand the outreach. The report warns that the street's veterans deserved persistent help. The programs had to reach them.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-659: The Fed's auction computers needed securing in 2006, and GAO's report says the Federal Reserve had to address the Treasury auction systems. The findings target the vulnerabilities. The report warns that the nation's debt sales needed locked-down tech. The systems had to be secure.
gao-gaoreports-b-298259: Southwest Educational Development Laboratory took its July 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The lab said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Research outfits get the same full hearing as all.
gao-gaoreports-b-297959: NCR Government Systems doubled its May 2006 protest — two case numbers, one tech fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-259: Immigration benefit fraud needed more controls in 2006, and GAO's report says additional safeguards and a sanctions strategy could enhance DHS's control. The findings demand the tools. The report warns that the benefit pipeline should not leak. The controls had to be added.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-59: Medicare therapy payments were poorly targeted in 2005, and GAO's report says little progress had been made in matching payments to needs. The findings target the waste. The report warns that the patients deserved needs-based care. The progress had to come.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-859: The visa process needed staffing and sharing in 2005, and GAO's report says improvements in personnel and information exchange would help. The findings demand the upgrades. The report warns that the borders deserved well-run gates. The improvements had to come.
openalex-w7205005059: Radishes are simple, but growing them well takes science. This agronomy study tested how different levels of shade affect radish growth in the soil and climate of western Amazonia. Conducted at the Federal University of Acre, the experiment measured which shade conditions produced the best crop. A small, concrete piece of agricultural research with direct value for farmers working under the Amazon sun.
openalex-w7205009059: Future science teachers learn their craft partly in real classrooms through Brazil's PIBID program. This study asks students in 7th and 8th grade what they thought of those trainee teachers and how well theory met practice in their science lessons. The authors measure the impact on learning and on the trainees' growth. A ground-level view of teacher training where the judges are the teenagers.
openalex-w7204461359: Government agencies need plans, not just reactions. This article studies the upsides of strategic planning in Brazil's indirect public administration, the state-run bodies that manage public interests. Based on descriptive research and literature review, the authors argue that structured planning serves the public mission better. A management study for readers who believe bureaucracy can be steered.
openalex-w7204463159: The Amazon holds a dazzling share of the world's orchids, and this study takes their census. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the orchid family in Amazonas state: species, endemics, hybrids, pollination, and conservation, using data current to mid-2026. A botanical overview as rich as its subject, and a baseline for protecting it.
openalex-w7204232059: Deepfakes poison the information well, and this paper proposes a defense. The authors present ETHOS-SE, a socio-technical framework for fighting AI-generated disinformation: part detection tech, part social design. They address the gap between lab advances and real-world trust. A forward-looking study of defending truth in the synthetic age.
openalex-w7204757659: Bones and teeth build themselves from calcium phosphate, and labs want to copy the trick. This review covers biomineralization-inspired routes to functional bioceramics. The authors surveyed how body-fluid chemistry guides the growth. A biomaterials review of nature's building code.
arxiv-2606-15959: Scientists often replace slow physics simulations with fast neural networks, but the training data can be huge, so compression helps. Lossy compression, however, throws away detail. This paper measures how much that data loss hurts the neural network's accuracy. The authors map the tradeoff so labs can shrink their datasets without losing the quality they need.
arxiv-2606-16059: Financial institutions are hungry for faster, cheaper AI. This paper presents Mojo, a programming language and toolchain, as a promising route to scalable, efficient financial AI — work aimed at the practice section of Communications of the ACM. It argues Mojo's speed and simplicity make it well suited to the heavy numerical workloads of modern finance.
arxiv-2606-16259: Most stuff eases to rest on a set clock — yet glassy stuff drags far past it. This paper proves such drag for the triangle-chip game (a toy magnet board), in any head-count of dims. For slow-physics fans who clock glassy crawl.
arxiv-2606-16659: Scammers text fake links that lead to phishing webpages. FraudSMSWalker is a benchmark testing whether agentic large language models can trace an SMS scam to its webpage and detect the fraud. It gives security researchers a standard test for AI agents fighting mobile phishing.
arxiv-2606-16859: Molecules absorb light and dance in excited states — simulating that dance is costly. This paper makes machine learning of excited-state dynamics transferable across molecules, using 'extremal pooling.' It is for computational chemists. Learn once, dance many. One model, many molecules.
